item.description: The with_suffix method has flawed path reconstruction logic for both absolute and relative URLs, particularly in handling cases where the path has no trailing slash or when paths are empty.
item.contract: The with_suffix method must correctly handle all URL types (absolute with netloc, absolute without netloc, relative) when modifying the file suffix. It should properly reconstruct paths to maintain correct URL structure, especially when dealing with empty paths or paths without trailing slashes.

item.description: The with_name method has incorrect path construction logic for relative URLs, particularly around handling leading slashes and path segments.
item.contract: The with_name method must properly handle all URL types when changing the name component. It should correctly construct paths for both absolute URLs (with netloc) and relative URLs (without netloc), ensuring proper path structure and leading slash handling.

item.description: The validation logic in with_suffix method incorrectly raises ValueError for URLs with empty names, causing failures in test cases that should succeed.
item.contract: The with_suffix method should properly validate when a name exists in the path before attempting to modify it, raising ValueError with appropriate message only when truly invalid (e.g., trying to modify suffix on a URL without a path component).

item.description: The with_suffix method doesn't correctly handle URLs with no path segments or empty paths (e.g., "http://example.com")
item.contract: The with_suffix method must handle URLs with no path segments gracefully, ensuring it properly constructs paths for absolute URLs that have no path component without throwing errors.

item.description: The with_name method has issues with edge cases involving empty paths and relative paths, causing incorrect path construction.
item.contract: The with_name method should correctly handle edge cases including empty paths and relative paths, ensuring it properly constructs the new path regardless of URL type and preserves proper path structure.
